parties.popularity_note: No national vote since its founding; 1996 National Assembly vote shares of its two founding parties, the New Korea Party (34.52%) and the United Democratic Party (11.23%), are summed. Lee Hoi-chang won 38.75% as its 1997 presidential candidate.
parties.note: One record covers the Grand National Party (1997-2012), its renaming to the Saenuri Party (2012) and to the Liberty Korea Party (2017); Wikipedia treats them as one article. It merged with the New Conservative Party and Onward for Future 4.0 on 17 February 2020 to form the United Future Party. Acting chairs and some short emergency committees (2016-2017) are omitted from leader_history.

parties.note: Kim Dae-jung's party, governing in coalition with the United Liberal Democrats in January 2000. On 20 January 2000 it merged with Lee In-je's New People Party and others to become the Millennium Democratic Party.

parties.note: Renamed Democratic Party on 6 May 2005. Roh Moo-hyun's supporters left to form the Uri Party in 2003. In June 2007 the remaining party merged with the Central Reform United New Party into a new Democratic Party (2007), which joined the United Democratic Party in February 2008; that intermediate party is folded into this lineage.

parties.note: Formed by supporters of President Roh Moo-hyun who left the Millennium Democratic Party; won 152 of 299 seats in 2004. Merged into the Grand Unified Democratic New Party in August 2007. Wikipedia gives foundation as 1 November 2003; Wikidata gives 11 November 2003.

parties.note: Founded by Cho Kuk; won 12 list seats in 2024. Cho Kuk's second spell was acting from 8 September 2025 until his election on 23 November 2025 (the leader list gives 11 September 2025 as its start). Acting leaders between spells (Kim Joon-hyung, Kim Sun-min, and Shin Jang-sik from 4 June 2026) are omitted. Shin Jang-sik was elected leader on 25 July 2026 (Wikipedia, citing the Chosun Ilbo of 25 July 2026).
